honestyAlert.text: Operating manuals for this documentation class. The chapters describe in clear US English what the product does today. They are not a System Security Plan, a FedRAMP package, or a certification claim — map controls in your binder to the evidence you actually collect.

intro.text: Manuals are activated according to RBAC documentation class. Each class contains usable chapters for daily work. Super Administrators see every class. Technical OpenAPI access also requires membership in the well-known Developer (or Super Administrator) group. These pages are not a certification package — keep SSP credentials in the assessment binder.

summary.text: How to set up auditors on the same sign-in page, which groups to use, and where to change settings.

0.text: Everyone logs in to the same login page. There is no separate examiner portal. Menus and rights come from the groups you assign. This corresponds to the Thoropass model: an examiner examines evidence; An audit administrator (management) can also set up other auditors. Identity administrators create accounts that are not validators. This is not the job of an auditor.

1.text: Demonstration environments include three starting accounts so you can try out each task. Change these passwords before each joint demonstration. Production environments create their own people and assign them to the groups below. This guide describes how to set up the product. It is not a certification claim.

0.text: Open the local IAM administration and create or select the person.

1.text: Add the person to the groups for their role in the table below.

2.text: Or create them with the matching enrollment template.

3.text: Ask them to sign in on the normal sign-in page.

4.text: Open audit engagements to invite them to an engagement if your process uses invitations.

Managed identities are local accounts on a chosen endpoint whose passwords are rotated by the server. First choose an endpoint — identities are always machine-related. The credential vault stores secrets for session and access flows. Treat vault lines as sensitive inventory, not as evidence that your organization's password policy is met.

Each creation and redemption should appear under Compliance & Evidence → Audit Trail.

summary.text: Connection points, jump capacity, recordings, command filtering and session approvals.

body[0].text: Brokered access brokers recorded SSH, RDP and related sessions. Connection points define goals. Session controls and session recordings show live and saved session evidence. Recording Ops includes recording agent health, deployment, RDP OCR/metadata and recording storage. Permissions and session I/O policies decide who can open which targets and which I/O rules apply.

body[1].text: Jump & Capacity → Jump Fleet & Load Balancing configures Jump/Recording Proxy capacity across external Jump hosts and the local AIC server endpoint. Use Check Placement for a dry run selection of the least loaded node — the does not open a user session. SSH Command Filtering under Brokered Access → Policy controls which commands a brokered SSH session is allowed to execute when a filter is bound. A permitted command that succeeds and a restricted command that is rejected are the live evidence of this policy. summary.text: Service health, encryption backup and restore, and post-change auditing.

body[0].text: After deployments or configuration changes, ensure you ensure HTTPS health and that your admin session is still working. Check compliance & evidence → audit trail for unexpected errors. Configuration → Server → Service Logs helps check service-side log output in the event of startup or runtime problems.

body[1].text: Configuration → Security → Encryption Settings includes backup and restore for encryption material (export, import and optional super admin plain text export if your role allows it). Encryption key sets cover the server standard and named master encryption keys, including rotating and re-encrypting after key changes. These bottles protect cryptographic custody - they are not a complete application database backup device. Have an external recovery path available for PostgreSQL and host configuration before performing a destructive database initialization.

body[2].text: After a large deployment or a destructive database initialization, verify that endpoint enrollment, password recovery, and the elevation channel are still working before treating the system as ready. Never perform a destructive database initialization without first preparing a recovery path.
